questiontext.text:
Each expansion below is written in descending powers of \(x\) (the highest power of \(x\) first). Without expanding fully, choose the pattern of the signs of its coefficients.

  1. \({@shown[1]@}\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
  2. \({@shown[2]@}\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]
  3. \({@shown[3]@}\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]
  4. \({@shown[4]@}\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Look at the sign of the highest power of \(x\) and of the next term. A minus sign between the two terms of the bracket makes the signs alternate. An odd power of \(-x\) is negative and an even power is positive, and \((-x - c)^m = (-1)^m(x + c)^m\).

  1. \({@shown[1]@} = {@EX[perm[1]]@}\): {@catn[perm[1]]@}.
  2. \({@shown[2]@} = {@EX[perm[2]]@}\): {@catn[perm[2]]@}.
  3. \({@shown[3]@} = {@EX[perm[3]]@}\): {@catn[perm[3]]@}.
  4. \({@shown[4]@} = {@EX[perm[4]]@}\): {@catn[perm[4]]@}.

questiondescription.text:
Binomial Expansions: sign patterns in binomial expansions

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.2: Classify the sign pattern of four binomial expansions in descending powers of x without expanding them fully.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: For \({@it2@}\) you chose Alternate, starting with +. In descending powers of \(x\) the first term is \((-x)^3\). Is an odd power of \(-x\) positive or negative?

node.description: Even power of a negative bracket

truefeedback.text: For \({@it3@}\) you chose All negative. Take the minus sign out of the bracket: \((-x - {@c3@})^{@m3@} = (-1)^{@m3@}(x + {@c3@})^{@m3@}\). What does the even power \({@m3@}\) do to \(-1\)?

falsefeedback.text: You have \({@nc@}\) of the 4 right. For each bracket, work out the sign of the highest power of \(x\) and of the next term; a minus sign between the terms makes the signs alternate.

qtest.description: Even power of a negative bracket
